bank_evidence: CNROM (mapper 3) active bank is a write-only runtime latch not exposed by fceumm; inferred VISUALLY. The live Big Wave surfer metasprite (exact OAM tile/attr/x/y) was composed from each of the 4 CHR banks (sprite pattern table PT0 = PPU $0000, per PPUCTRL 0x90 bit3=0) and compared pixel-for-pixel to a crop of the live framebuffer at the metasprite's screen bbox. Bank 2 matches exactly (idle AND a 23-sprite carve frame both reproduced); banks 0/1 are incoherent noise, bank 3 renders a different (wrong) body. vram_to_rom could not corroborate: the CHR pattern tables are not a live-readable region on this core (only PPUREG/NTARAM/PALRAM/OAM are), so content-match provenance is unavailable.

notes.street_skate: CONTRADICTS the prior tcsurfdesign.md claim. Live PPU OAM in Street Skate (mode 0, gate=$04) shows a ~17-sprite skater metasprite (OAM slots 5-21, tiles 0x41-0x74) clustered exactly at the on-screen skater (x104-136,y120-152) — the skater IS OAM sprites here, NOT background-rendered. The doc/brief "zero player OAM sprites in Street" was not reproduced at the skate-segment START; it may have described a later auto-scroll phase. Flagged TO-VERIFY; not part of the swap scope this pass.
notes.wood_water: Mode 2 (Wood & Water Rage) OPENS on a skate segment visually identical to Street (same ~17-sprite skater metasprite, tiles 0x41-0x74) — NOT the surfer. Its surf segment was not reached this session (TO-VERIFY). Per the doc roster-sharing finding, the Wood surf segment is expected to reuse the Big Wave surfer tiles+bank, but that was not confirmed live.
notes.surfer_A_vs_B: Surfer A ($704=0, A-pedestal) and Surfer B ($704=1) SHARE the same sprite tile set in bank 2 (168 of As tiles are identical to Bs; A and B differ by only 2 rarely-seen tiles = sampling noise). They are distinguished PURELY BY PALETTE: PALRAM sprite subpalettes 4/6/7 differ. Most visibly the board color lives in subpalette 7 index2 — A uses $16 (red), B uses $2a (green). Subpalettes recorded at top level are Surfer As; Surfer Bs live subpalettes (opaque colors) are 4:[#4CD020,#D48820,#000000] 6:[#000000,#D48820,#ECEEEC] 7:[#000000,#4CD020,#ECEEEC] (subpalette 5 identical to A). A tile swap therefore reskins BOTH surfers at once.
notes.anim_bytes: $0400-$0407 = 589804d000143cf0 is STATIC across every Big Wave pose and identical for A and B (it is NOT a per-pose animation key here, contra the session-1 doc guess that $0400-$0405 are the player metasprite/animation tile indices). The Big Wave metasprite is driven by wave momentum + input over continuous play, not by this byte range; poses are identified by the normalized OAM (tile,attr,dx,dy) set instead.
notes.pose_method: Player sprites in Big Wave = ALL active OAM sprites except slot 0 (a parked tile-0xFF junk sprite at x0/y190). The surfer is screen-ANCHORED on the wave, so the poke-$478/$48C identity test from the doc does NOT apply (both are re-derived each frame in Big Wave and the metasprite does not translate with them). Identity instead rests on: (a) all active sprites cluster tightly at the surfer, (b) NO active OAM sprite ever appeared outside that cluster across a ~40s ride (nonplayer_oam scan = empty for both A and B), (c) the composed metasprite matches the live framebuffer. A POSE = distinct normalized (tile,attr,dx,dy) set; the metasprite animates continuously (~165-172 distinct configs seen per character over a 40s ride, ~25-28 of them single-cluster). The reference_captures are 6 curated single-cluster representatives per character spanning the sprite-count range (tuck=10, idle/base=19, carve=20/23/25/26 sprites).
notes.bank_method: render_tiles source=rom_file:chr offset=bank*8192 (PT0) with palette=live:7, composed via the metasprite compose logic (index0 transparent, high-OAM-slot drawn first so low slots land on top, honoring attr flip bits 0x40/0x80), compared to sips-crop of app://screen.
notes.palette_method: Live PALRAM read via read_region(region_name="PALRAM",offset=0,len=32); sprite subpalettes are bytes 16-31 (4 subpalettes x 4 bytes; index0 transparent). NES master-palette index -> RGB via the frontend NES_MASTER_PALETTE (src/mcp/snapshot.rs).
notes.tile_sharing_scan: GATE RESULT — VERDICT: the Big Wave surfer is CLEANLY SWAPPABLE. (1) OAM: across a ~40s ride for BOTH A and B, the ONLY active OAM sprites were the surfer metasprite plus the inert slot-0 tile-0xFF junk sprite; zero foreign sprites referenced the surfer tiles (nonplayer_oam scan empty), so tiles_shared_with_nonplayer=[] within the mode. (2) NTARAM: 810 of 2048 background nametable cells hold an INDEX that also appears in the surfer tile set, BUT this is FALSE collateral: PPUCTRL=0x90 has bit4=1 so the background uses pattern table 1 ($1000), while sprites use pattern table 0 ($0000). A nametable value V references physical CHR at bank_base+$1000+V*$10, whereas the surfer sprite tile V is at bank_base+V*$10 — DISJOINT physical bytes within the 8KB bank. Rendering bank2 PT1 confirms it holds the HUD font ("0123456789 POINT SURF LIFE") and wave tiles, not surfer art. Swapping the surfer PT0 tiles (bank2 $0000-$0FFF) cannot touch the HUD/wave graphics (bank2 $1000-$1FFF). CAVEAT: the swap edits shared CHR bytes, so it reskins BOTH surfer A and B (same tiles, palette-differentiated) and, if bank 2 is reused by the Wood surf segment, that segment too.
notes.scope: This pass covers mode 1 (Big Wave), both surfers, on the fceumm core, ROM sha1 7114bc8b. Player CHR bank inferred visually (bank 2). All addresses/facts are live-probed on port 4028.
